title: Ultimate-Chicken Kurkure
description: Chicken Kurkure is a crispy, restaurant-style chicken appetizer with a crunchy golden coating, juicy flavorful chicken inside, and perfectly balanced spices. It is served hot with mint chutney, spicy mayo, or ketchup for a delicious restaurant-style experience.

ingredients.title: For Marination
items: Boneless chicken – 250g (cut into thin finger-sized strips)

ingredients.title: For Coating
items: Chili powder – a pinch (optional, for extra heat)

instruction.title: Step 1: Marinate the Chicken
steps: Place the chicken strips in a bowl.
Add ginger-garlic paste, chopped green chilies, coriander powder, Kashmiri chili powder, black pepper, garam masala, lemon juice or vinegar, and salt.
Add yogurt if using for extra tenderness.
Mix thoroughly until the chicken is evenly coated.
Cover and marinate for 30–60 minutes. For best flavor, refrigerate and marinate longer.

instruction.title: Step 2: Prepare the Coating
steps: In a shallow bowl, combine corn flour, all-purpose flour, and breadcrumbs.
Add a pinch of salt and chili powder if desired.
Mix well so the coating ingredients are evenly distributed.

instruction.title: Step 3: Coat the Chicken
steps: Take each marinated chicken strip and coat it thoroughly in the flour-breadcrumb mixture.
Press the coating gently onto the chicken so it adheres well.
For extra crunch, lightly dip the coated strip in a little water or yogurt and coat it again in the dry mixture.
Place the coated chicken strips on a tray and let them rest for 5–10 minutes.

instruction.title: Step 4: Frying
steps: Heat oil to approximately 170–175°C over medium heat.
Fry the chicken strips in batches without overcrowding the pan.
Fry for about 3–4 minutes per batch, or until golden brown, crispy, and fully cooked.
Maintain the oil temperature so the coating becomes crisp without burning.
Drain the fried chicken on a wire rack or paper towels.

instruction.title: Step 5: Finishing Touch
steps: Sprinkle chaat masala over the hot Chicken Kurkure.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve with lemon wedges.
Serve immediately with mint chutney, spicy mayo, or ketchup.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve hot with mint chutney or spicy mayo.
Pair with lemon wedges for a fresh, tangy contrast.
Serve with ketchup for a simple family-style option.
For a restaurant-style presentation, arrange the crispy chicken strips neatly on a white plate and serve the dip in a small bowl.
Garnish with fresh coriander and a light sprinkle of chaat masala.

chefTips: Yogurt trick – Add 1 tbsp yogurt to the marinade to keep the chicken tender and juicy.
Double coating – Dip the first-coated chicken lightly in water or yogurt and coat again for a thicker, crunchier crust.
Corn flour + maida – Keep the ratio around 2:1 for a crisp, light coating.
Breadcrumbs – Use coarse breadcrumbs for a more textured and crunchy exterior.
Oil control – Maintain the oil around 170–175°C; oil that is too hot can burn the coating while oil that is too cool can make it greasy.
Avoid overcrowding – Fry in small batches so the oil temperature stays stable and the chicken becomes evenly crisp.
Juicy chicken – Chicken thigh strips are naturally more tender, while breast strips should not be overcooked.
Serve immediately – Chicken Kurkure is at its crispiest when served hot and fresh.
